contract.name: wcag-aa
contract.calibratedFor: Anyone: WCAG 2.x level AA is a published standard, calibrated for no one person's eyes, screen or room.

text.why: WCAG 2.x SC 1.4.3 (level AA) asks 4.5:1 of text at normal size, and these pairs are body copy, links and the labels on fills, read at any size.
text.retire: Wrong once the standard a product is judged by stops measuring body text with this ratio, or if every one of these pairs were only ever set large and bold, which owes 3:1.

text-subtle.why: `text-subtle` paints what is not body copy — placeholders, separators, icons and the hints beside a control — and is held to the 3:1 WCAG 2.x AA asks of large text and of non-text marks (SC 1.4.3, SC 1.4.11).
text-subtle.retire: Wrong the day `text-subtle` is the colour of text a reader needs at normal size, which WCAG holds to 4.5:1; input placeholders are the closest it comes today.

scrim.why: Text over the scrim is text at normal size (SC 1.4.3) and a promise about ANY image behind it, so the ratio held to 4.5:1 is the worst the translucent scrim can come to, anywhere between its composite over white and its composite over black.
scrim.retire: Wrong if the scrim becomes opaque (its pairs are then ordinary `text`), or if nothing set over it is ever text.

control-border.why: WCAG 2.x SC 1.4.11 (level AA) asks 3:1 of the visual information needed to identify a control, and `border-strong` is the edge that says where an input is.
control-border.retire: Wrong if inputs gain another boundary that clears 3:1 by itself (a fill, say), which leaves the border decorative and outside SC 1.4.11.

shape.why: WCAG 2.x SC 1.4.11 (level AA) asks 3:1 of a graphic that carries meaning with no label beside it, and the `-solid` colours paint exactly those: checkbox fills, slider tracks, tab indicators, switch tracks, spinners and the edge of a pastel button.
shape.retire: Wrong if a `-solid` colour stops being the whole of the shape: every such affordance labelled, or outlined in a colour that clears the floor itself.

focus.why: The focus ring is the only sign of where the keyboard is (SC 2.4.7), and as a non-text indicator it owes 3:1 to what it is drawn against (SC 1.4.11).
focus.retire: Wrong if the ring is drawn against anything but `bg` and `surface`, or becomes a two-colour ring that shows on any background, which one ratio no longer describes.

chart.why: Chart marks are non-text UI and owe 3:1 (SC 1.4.11), which light mode meets; dark mode's usable lightness band (about 0.48–0.67 OKLCH L) cannot always reach it on the dark surfaces, so the floor there is 2.25 and every Chart ships a legend, tooltips and a table view as the relief.
chart.retire: The dark 2.25 is wrong the day a dark palette can reach 3:1 inside the band the colour-vision gate needs (raise it to 3), or the day a Chart ships without its legend, tooltips and table view.
